planting.note: Plant container stock in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun; this very low, flat grower is widely used as a gold-sport parent, including Mother Lode juniper.

directions: Wiltonii, also sold as Blue Rug juniper, is an extremely low, flat-growing selection of creeping juniper valued for its dense mat of trailing stems covered in fine, silvery-blue scale-like foliage that hugs the ground closely enough to suppress most weeds once established. It has long served as a parent and sport source for other low gold- and blue-toned groundcover junipers. Tolerant of poor, sandy, or rocky soil and reflected heat, it is a staple for slopes, retaining-wall tops, and other spots too dry or exposed for most groundcovers. It needs no pruning beyond removing occasional upright reversion shoots.

common_name: Ruby Regis Annual Mallow (Cerise-Pink Rose Mallow)

planting.note: Direct sow after the last frost once soil has warmed, since this fast-growing annual mallow resents root disturbance.

directions: Ruby Regis is a deeper-colored companion to the better-known white Mont Blanc and pink-flushed Silver Cup in the Lavatera trimestris annual mallow group, bearing large, satiny, cerise-pink, hibiscus-like flowers on a bushy, well-branched mound of soft green foliage. Like its siblings it flowers continuously from early summer to frost on a single season's growth from seed. Thin seedlings to their final spacing early, pinch young plants once to encourage branching, and deadhead spent flowers to extend bloom. It makes a quick, colorful filler for borders or informal hedging.

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions into permanently moist, acidic peat in early spring, pairing female clones with a nearby male pollinizer such as Apollen or Apolto.

directions: Fjordgull is a female fruiting clone from Norway's long-running cloudberry breeding and clone-evaluation program at the Bioforsk research institute (now NIBIO), released alongside the related female clone Fjellgull and male pollinators Apollen and Apolto to make this wild Scandinavian bog fruit viable in managed plantings. It produces the species' characteristic amber-gold, tart, musky-flavored berries and was selected for heavier, more consistent fruit set than unselected wild clones. As a strictly dioecious species, it sets no fruit without a male clone blooming nearby. It demands cold winters and constantly waterlogged, acidic peat, and the very soft ripe berries must be hand-picked promptly since they bruise easily.

planting.note: Plant divisions as a pollen source among several female cloudberry clones such as Fjordgull or Fjellgull, since Rubus chamaemorus is strictly dioecious.

directions: Apolto is a male pollinator clone from Norway's Bioforsk (now NIBIO) cloudberry breeding program, released alongside the male clone Apollen and the female clones Fjellgull and Fjordgull. It produces no fruit of its own, serving purely to supply pollen with a bloom window timed to overlap its paired female clones in cold bog plantings. Give it the same constantly moist, acidic peat required by fruiting cloudberry, and space male plants at a ratio of roughly one to several females for dependable pollination.

planting.note: Plant grafted trees in deep, well-drained soil in full sun; this early-twentieth-century natural hican bears a large nut but is a collector's or breeding-program tree rather than a reliable commercial producer.

directions: Burlington is an early-twentieth-century natural hican, a pecan x shellbark hickory cross (Carya x nussbaumeri) long kept in cultivation mainly through nut-collector grafting rather than commercial orchards. It produces a large, shellbark-influenced nut and has historically been compared with other old named hicans of similar parentage. Bearing tends to be light and inconsistent compared with modern pecan cultivars, so it is best treated as an historic curiosity or breeding-program tree rather than a dependable home-orchard choice. Give it the same deep, well-drained orchard conditions used for pecan and shellbark hickory, and expect a long juvenile period before the first nuts.

common_name: Rock Master Hosta (Historic Aden Breeding Parent)

planting.note: Divide established clumps in spring or plant container stock in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Rock Master is a hosta cultivar from pioneering hybridizer Paul Aden, whose main documented legacy today is as a breeding parent, crossed with the dwarf species Hosta venusta to produce Shining Tot, itself later a parent of the miniature gold-leaved Shiny Penny. Like other hostas it forms a clump of foliage from a crown that spreads slowly by offsets rather than running stolons. Plant divisions in early fall or spring, keep soil consistently moist through summer heat, and mulch to protect the crown over winter.
sources: Green Hill Farm hosta breeding history notes

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade, where blue leaf color is deepest and longest-lasting.

directions: Blue Dimples is a small, blue-leaved hosta cultivar best known today as the parent that produced a spontaneous gold-colored sport later developed into the miniature Appletini. It forms a compact mound of the glaucous, waxy-coated foliage typical of blue hostas, which fades toward green as the protective bloom wears off through the season. Grow in consistently moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full shade, since sun and heat accelerate the loss of blue coloring. Divide clumps in spring or early fall as needed.
sources: Green Hill Farm hosta breeding history notes

common_name: Jade Cascade Hosta (Mint Rushmore Breeding Parent)

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, allowing generous room for a large, slow-building clump.

directions: Jade Cascade is a large, green-leaved hosta cultivar used by breeders Monty and Julie Carlson as one of the parents, together with Komodo Dragon, Bright Lights, and Lakeside Delight, in crosses aimed at producing the giant minty-green hosta Mint Rushmore. It carries the substantial, gently arching leaf habit implied by its name, building slowly into an imposing clump over several seasons rather than filling in quickly. Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, and give it ample room to reach full size undisturbed.
sources: Regional hosta society breeding program notes

common_name: Tongue Twister Hosta (Green Hill Farm Blue Breeding Line)

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade, where blue foliage color holds best.

directions: Tongue Twister is a blue-leaved hosta cultivar from Bob Solberg's Green Hill Farm breeding program, used as a parent alongside Iwa and Blue Blush in the cross that produced the ruffled, pointed-leaf Buttonwood Bay. It forms the clump of waxy, glaucous blue foliage typical of hostas in this breeding line, with color holding best in consistent shade. Grow in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, and divide in spring or early fall once the clump becomes crowded.
sources: Green Hill Farm hosta breeding history notes

common_name: Summer Squall Hosta (Green Hill Farm Blue Breeding Line)

planting.note: Plant divisions in evenly moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade for the best color retention through the season.

directions: Summer Squall is a blue-leaved hosta from Bob Solberg's Green Hill Farm 'Longiana' breeding line, used as a parent with Fragrant Blue to produce the upright, long-holding Clear Blue Sky. It carries the clean, crisp blue coloring characteristic of this breeding line, which tends to hold through the season longer than many other blue hostas before fading toward green. Grow in evenly moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade, and divide established clumps in spring or early fall.
sources: Green Hill Farm hosta breeding history notes

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in part shade with some morning sun to encourage spring red blushing.

directions: Swoosh is one of the yellow, red-blushing hosta cultivars from Doug Ruff's breeding line, bred toward producing the narrow, wavy leaves that emerge bright yellow with red blushing near the leaf margins, a group popularized commercially as the 'blushing' hostas. It was used as a parent, crossed with Raving Beauty and then onto First Blush, in the line that produced Light the Match. The red blush fades as summer heat builds, leaving a persistent yellow base color. Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in part shade with some morning sun to encourage the spring blush.
sources: Walters Gardens hosta breeding program notes

common_name: Raving Beauty Hosta (Yellow Blushing-Red Breeding Line)

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in part shade with some morning sun to encourage spring red blushing.

directions: Raving Beauty is part of Doug Ruff's yellow, red-blushing hosta breeding line, sharing the narrow, wavy leaves that emerge bright yellow with red tinting running from the leaf tips toward the base, fading to a persistent yellow base color by midsummer. It was crossed with Swoosh and then onto First Blush to produce Light the Match, one of the first hostas descended from this 'blushing' breeding line. Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in part shade with some morning sun, which intensifies the spring blush, and divide clumps in spring or fall as needed.
sources: Walters Gardens hosta breeding program notes

common_name: Potomac Pride Hosta (Classic Dark Green Breeding Parent)

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade, where the dark leaf color is deepest and glossiest.

directions: Potomac Pride is a classic hosta cultivar noted for broad, glossy, very dark green leaves, among the darkest available in the genus, which can read as nearly black in low shade-garden light. It has long been used as a breeding parent, including a cross with Neat Splash Rim that produced the near-black Midnight Oil. The glossy leaf surface helps the dark color read as rich rather than dull, distinguishing it from matte dark-leaved hostas. Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in shade, where color and shine are both most pronounced, and divide established clumps as needed.
sources: Regional hosta society breeding program notes

common_name: Neat Splash Rim Hosta (Classic Variegated-Margin Breeding Parent)

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in part to full shade, where variegation contrast holds best.

directions: Neat Splash Rim is a classic hosta cultivar belonging to the Splash Rim group of margin-variegated hostas, carrying a lighter, irregular border splashed along the edge of each leaf. It has served as a breeding parent, including a cross with Potomac Pride that produced the near-black Midnight Oil, pairing its variegation genetics with darker-leaved lines. Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in part to full shade, since strong sun can scorch the lighter variegated tissue, and divide crowded clumps in spring or early fall.
sources: Regional hosta society breeding program notes

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in part shade, giving a large, slow-building clump ample room.

directions: Brutus is a large hosta cultivar from breeders D. and M. Beilstein in the Hosta montana breeding group, known for the extremely thick, heavy-substance leaves that style is bred for. It was crossed with Clear Fork River Valley and a Brutus x Hosta montana f. macrophylla seedling to produce Hogwarts, which inherited the group's dense, textured foliage. Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in part shade, and give the clump several years and generous room to reach its full, substantial size.
sources: Regional hosta society breeding program notes

common_name: Clear Fork River Valley Hosta (Montana-Type Breeding Parent)

planting.note: Plant divisions in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in part shade, giving a large, slow-building clump ample room.

directions: Clear Fork River Valley is a large hosta cultivar from breeders D. and M. Beilstein, part of the same Hosta montana-type breeding effort that produced the thick-leaved Brutus. It was crossed with Brutus and a Hosta montana f. macrophylla seedling to produce Hogwarts, known for extremely thick, dark green, wart-textured leaves, a trait consistent with this breeding group's focus on heavy leaf substance. Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in part shade, and allow several seasons for the clump to reach its full, large size.
sources: Regional hosta society breeding program notes
